rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Rana tigrina, the amphibian type specimen, is a nocturnal, poikilothermic carnivore of water and moist land that hibernates and aestivates in mud. Its head and trunk carry bulging eyes with nictitating membranes, a tympanum behind each eye, and a wide mouth with vomerine and maxillary teeth and a bifid protrusible tongue; the moist glandular skin breathes cutaneously.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Mouth, pharynx, oesophagus, stomach, duodenum, ileum, rectum, cloaca.
Male external signs in season: vocal sac and nuptial pad.
Bile emulsifies. Pepsin and pancreatic protease digest protein. Amylase digests starch. Lipase digests fat.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The frog chews with nothing. Maxillary and vomerine teeth only grip. The lower jaw has no teeth.  ·  The tongue is hinged at the front, not at the back. A diagram with the root at the throat is a mammal's tongue.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The course name is Rana tigrina. Newer genus names are not required in an answer that asks for the type animal.  ·  Tadpole feeding and gills belong to metamorphosis, not to this adult digestive account.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Rana tigrina*** — Indian bullfrog; type specimen of Amphibia.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Heart and respiration are the next note. Reproductive organs of the frog are a later topic and are not written here.  ·  Enzyme names are limited to pepsin, pancreatic protease, amylase and lipase, plus bile as a non-enzyme.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Sketch the head and mark tympanum, nostril, eye and the male characters.  ·  Make a four-row digestion table: mouth, stomach, duodenum, ileum.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Four fingers, five toes, webbed feet, no neck."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** What is the cloaca? **Answer.** A **common posterior chamber** into which the intestine, the urinary ducts and the reproductive ducts all open; it exits to the exterior through the cloacal aperture. Frog, like other amphibians, retains this single exit for faeces, urine and gametes.

rows.text: No verified PYQ in the bank; practise external features and alimentary canal as NEB-style practice.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Amphibian duality:** every system reflects the double life — lungs plus skin respiration, webbed limbs plus jumping legs, water-bound reproduction.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Habitat: amphibious, nocturnal, hibernates/aestivates; poikilothermic; cutaneous respiration.  ·  External: head + trunk, no neck; nictitating membrane; tympanum; 4 fingers (male nuptial pad), webbed hind toes; cloaca; male vocal sacs.  ·  Digestive: buccopharyngeal cavity with vomerine/maxillary teeth + bifid protrusible tongue → short oesophagus → stomach (HCl, pepsin) → intestine with liver + pancreas (bile, pancreatic juice) → large intestine → cloaca.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The frog's tongue attach point is at the front of the mouth — it flips out tip-first.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The cloaca is not an anus. Faeces, urine and gametes share it.  ·  Hibernation and aestivation are both dormancy. One answers cold, the other answers heat and drought.  ·  Sexual dimorphism (nuptial pad, vocal sacs) is a favourite 2m item.
